title: nail search panics on a query file whose first line is blank
body:
`guess_query_format_from_query_file` in `nail/src/util.rs` picks the query format from the file's first line. `search` calls it at `nail/src/search.rs:51`. It reads the first line into a `String` and compares fixed-length slices of it:

```rust
if &first_line[0..1] == ">" {
    Ok(FileFormat::Fasta)
} else if &first_line[0..11] == "# STOCKHOLM" {
    Ok(FileFormat::Stockholm)
} else if &first_line[0..5] == "HMMER" {
```

A first line shorter than a slice panics. A HMMER3 file whose first line is blank gives `first_line == "\n"`, and the `[0..11]` slice panics:

```text
indexing query database...
The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  end byte index 11 is out of bounds for string of length 1
Location: nail/src/util.rs:85
```

The report came against nail 0.7.1, with the Pfam model `AAA_16` (`PF13191.3`) from http://www.repeatmasker.org/~rhubley/blank_first_line.hmm. I reproduced it on dev at `326797b`, with a release build from Oct 17. `util.rs` has not changed since `b11b071`. With the blank line removed, the same file runs to completion.

By reading the code, an empty query file panics at the `[0..1]` slice. A first line of 1 to 10 bytes that does not start with `>` panics at `[0..11]`. Neither case has been run.

`Profile::from_p7hmm` drops empty lines before parsing, so the parser likely accepts this file. Nobody has checked the record indexer in `nail/src/io/p7hmm.rs` against a leading blank line.

## Open

- Should detection skip leading blank lines, or reject the file with a message that names it?
